decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already records the required E and L cap-height alignment to the second V's left arm; no additional update or removal is needed.
The source changes E and L scale relative to the second V, not their architectural construction, originality, or design language.
The hierarchy change uses the Hero V only as an existing reference and does not alter its locked geometry or current rules.
The client retains and verifies the common baseline in the same message; the second V cap-height hierarchy does not change the baseline rule.
The source keeps the second V geometry intact and adjusts the surrounding E and L scale and visual hierarchy rather than changing the glyph's proportional-reduction construction.
The same message separately selects Variation B with tighter kerning, which is already represented by a complete same-message MODIFY; the hierarchy change requires no further kerning update.
The source does not change the existing exact peak-alignment rule between the Hero V and É accent.
The request to preserve an exact Hero V right-arm copy for the accent reiterates the existing shared terminal rule and does not change its current state.
The perfect copy/paste instruction reiterates the already active one-to-one Hero V terminal derivation requirement without introducing a new value, removal, or scope change.
The source contains no decision about explanations or rationale accompanying design review rounds.
The typography hierarchy decision does not affect the deferred champagne material treatment.
The source does not concern proof attachment formats or Mac viewability.
